prerequisites: It is recommended to have studied Physics in 2nd year of high school and to have prior mathematical knowledge of vector calculus, trigonometry, and differentiation and integration of single-variable functions.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the concept of a wave and know its mathematical characterization as well as basic wave phenomena.
Know the basic concepts and laws of electromagnetism and apply them to the analysis of simple electromagnetic situations in vacuum and in material media.
Correctly handle the recommended physical symbolism, both in terms of magnitudes and units.
Learn and apply problem-solving strategies related to the different contents of the course.
Acquire skills related to laboratory work and the treatment of measurements and errors.

syllabus_topics: Electrostatics. Electric charge. Coulomb's Law. Electrostatic field and potential. Charge distributions. Electric dipole. Gauss's Law. Conductors. Capacitors. Electric field energy. Dielectrics.
Electric Current. Electric current intensity and density. Ohm's Law. Resistance. Joule effect. Generators: Electromotive force. DC circuits.

Magnetostatics. Magnetic field. Lorentz Law: Magnetic induction. Hall effect. Magnetic force on an electric current. Magnetic field moment on a loop. Biot-Savart Law. Force between currents. Ampere's Theorem. Magnetic field energy. Magnetism in matter.
Time-varying electromagnetic fields. Electromagnetic induction: Faraday-Henry Law. Self-induction. Maxwell's Equations. RLC circuits. Electrical oscillations.
Oscillations. Free oscillations. Damped oscillations. Forced oscillations.
Waves: Generalities. Mechanical waves. Concept of a wave. Wave differential equation. Wave classification. Harmonic waves. Mechanical waves. Wave phenomena. Doppler effect.
Practice 2. Capacitor Charging / Magnetic Field of a Solenoid.
Practice 4. Mechanical Waves / Standing Waves on a String.
teaching_methods: Exemplification of course content and solving typical problems by the professor
Presentation and defense of problems, assignments, projects
Handling measurement equipment in the laboratory
Use of simulation software and/or experimental data processing
Analysis of results and preparation of practice reports
Evaluation activities in very small groups
Study of theoretical-practical contents presented in the classroom and laboratory by the professor
Problem-solving and preparation of practice reports, assignments, etc., proposed by the professor for individual or group completion
Use of the University of Oviedo virtual platform
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, theory evaluation includes a mid-term exam (T1, min 5/10) and a second partial exam (T2, min 4/10) or a comprehensive theoretical exam (ET, min 4/10), plus class participation (PA). If T1 and T2 minimums are met, Theory = (0.35*T1) + (0.40*T2) + (0.10*PA); otherwise, Theory = (0.75*ET) + (0.10*PA). Practical evaluation requires at least 75% attendance and comprises practical work (P1) and a practical exam (P2), with Prácticas = (0.08*P1) + (0.07*P2). The final grade is the sum of the Theory and Practical scores; if minimums are not achieved or attendance is below 75%, the final grade is capped at 4.0. The extraordinary call involves a theoretical exam (ET, min 4/10) weighted 75% and maintained continuous evaluation (PA) at 10%. Practical work (P1) score is kept if attendance criteria were met; otherwise, a practical exam (P2, min 4/10) weighted 15% is required. The final grade is Theory + Practical, capped at 4.0 under certain conditions. Students under differentiated evaluation follow the extraordinary call criteria.
